newsitem.title: UK: IPE still hopes to launch gas contract this year.
newsitem.headline: IPE still hopes to launch gas contract this year.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) is still hoping to launch a forward natural gas contract this year but is unable to set a date, an IPE spokesman said on Friday.
"We have completed development work on the National Balancing Point (NBP) contract," Richard Ward, divisional director of business development at the IPE, told a conference on Friday.

He added that because all trades on the IPE are technically struck with the London Clearing House (LCH), which acts as an interface between buyers and sellers, the IPE must still finalise an agreement with industry regulator Ofgas over what role the LCH will play in the gas market.
"We still have to decide how the LCH will enter the cycle," he said. "Perhaps it will technically be licensed as a shipper".

He said he had a meeting on Thursday with Clare Spottiswoode, director general of Ofgas, to discuss the matter and now has to discuss it further with pipeline operator TransCo, a division of British Gas Plc.
Ward previously said he hoped the contract would start in November, but he was not specific about a possible launch date on Friday.

The NBP contract will offer three forward monthly trading periods and seven forward daily periods. Ward expects it to be used by traders looking to balance short-term physical needs, with nearly all trade resulting in physical delivery. By contrast the Bacton contract, which Ward now hopes to launch next year, will offer trade for 12 forward months as well as seven forward days. Ward expects it to be used mainly for paper trade, with deals cashed out rather than resulting in physical delivery, although that option will be available.
"We hope the Bacton contract will become the focus of price formation in the UK and will be used as the price benchmark."
